newsitem.title: USA: No High Court appeal in SEC case against broker.
newsitem.headline: No High Court appeal in SEC case against broker.

text.p: The U.S. Solicitor General's Office will not elevate to the Supreme Court the Securities and Exchange Commission's case against a former manager of PaineWebber Group Inc, the defendant's lawyer said on Friday.

Lawyer Arthur Hahn said from Chicago that the decision not to raise the case to the high court favors Patricia Johnson, who was accused by the SEC of alleged failure to properly supervised a broker who allegedly stole more than $114,000 from clients.
The SEC brought the case five-and-a-half years after Johnson's alleged infraction.
Johnson challenged the case, which the SEC brought in administrative or "in-house" proceeding, contending that the five-year statute of limitations had expired.
The SEC, ruling on the case, suspended Johnson from holding a supervisory position for six months. Johnson appealed to the U.S. Court of Appeals, which sided with her.
The SEC then asked the Solicitor General's Office to appeal the case to the Supreme Court.
Johnson now works as a broker with Smith Barney in California.
